'''It''' seems to be half starving.}} #* {{quote-newsgroup|en|date=31 December 2001|author=geek_girl|title=it is 10:23am and I am really drunk|newsgroup=alt.angst|url=https://groups.google.com/g/alt.angst/c/BebcfPo4WEQ/m/h0d3ri_Zr-0J|passage=> I bet you Sarah Jane talks to her dog on a daily basis. {{...}}

>
She is not an "'''it'''" she's a "her".}} #* {{quote-web |en |date=2018-08-06 |title=Brief Introduction of Nansi |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220216010128/https://nansi.tainan.gov.tw/en/cp.aspx?n=8337 |archivedate=16 February 2022 |work=Nansi District Office, Tainan City |text=The Nansi District was formerly known as the "Jiaba Community", and was one of the early territories of the Taivoan, as well as where the Zou resided. Later, due to the invasion of the Siraya tribe, the community members later migrated out to regions such as Gongguan, Paoziliao (Kaohsiung County), and Daciouyuan. During the time of the Japanese occupation, because of '''its''' location at the west of the "Nanzihsian River", '''it''' was therefore renamed Nansi ("si" meaning "west"). A village and village hall were established here, under the governance of Sinhua District of Tainan Province. After the war in 1945, '''it''' was renamed Nansi Township, and was changed to Nansi District after the merging of Tainan City and County on December 25th, 2010.}} ## {{non-gloss|Used to refer to a [[human]] generically, or humans collectively as a [[species]].}} ##* {{quote-newsgroup|en|date=11 March 2000|author=Gunner|title=A third of all murders unsolved.|newsgroup=misc.survivalism|url=https://groups.google.com/g/misc.survivalism/c/49bRka8eI9k/m/f6lIl95IY00J|passage=To kill a homo sapiens, in any of its life stages, is still killing a homo sapiens, no matter if '''it'''{{quote-gloss|'}}s sentient or not.}} ##* {{quote-newsgroup|en|date=2 April 2016|author=Nicodemus|title=[OT {{quote-gloss|off-topic}}]T{{sic}} what happens to a human when '''it''' realizes its place on planet earth|newsgroup=alt.comp.freeware|url=https://groups.google.com/g/alt.comp.freeware/c/b-g5k75HR_Q/m/Q3SzHiJ6IwAJ|nocolon=1}} ## {{lb|en|derogatory|offensive}} {{non-gloss|Used [[dehumanizingly]] to refer to a person.}} ##* {{quote-newsgroup|en|date=9 July 2002|author=Mark Shippey|title=The idiot still making a fool out of itself?|newsgroup=alt.alien.visitors|url=https://groups.google.com/g/alt.alien.visitors/c/EZzA3VglWU8/m/Spd8ewa_X-wJ|passage=My killfile has just about 100% obliterated the posts from the Erols goon. A few get through, but I'll bet the idiot is still sitting there spamming away and making a total fool out of itself. '''It''' has to, '''it''' has no other existence other than groveling for attention on Usenet. {{...}} Is it safe yet to release the erols domain from the killfile, or is '''IT''' still puking its putrid crap all over the groups in large amounts?}} # {{non-gloss|A third-person singular personal pronoun used to refer to a baby or child, especially of unknown gender.}} #: {{ux|en|She took the baby and held '''it''' in her arms.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1847|author=Charlotte Brontë|title=Jane Eyre|chapter=IV |passage=A child cannot quarrel with '''its''' elders, as I had done; cannot give '''its''' furious feelings uncontrolled play, as I had given mine, without experiencing afterwards the pang of remorse and the chill of reaction.}} #* {{RQ:Collins Woman in White|passage=I could only encourage Mrs. Clements to speak next of Anne's early days {{...}} "There was nobody else, sir, to take the little helpless creature in hand," replied Mrs. Clements. "The wicked mother seemed to hate '''it'''—as if the poor baby was in fault!—from the day '''it''' was born. My heart was heavy for the child, and I made the offer to bring '''it''' up as tenderly as if '''it''' was my own."
"Did Anne remain entirely under your care from that time?"
"Not quite entirely, sir. Mrs. Catherick had her whims and fancies about '''it''' at times, and used now and then to lay claim to the child, as if she wanted to spite me for bringing '''it''' up.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=Marcus Zusak|title=The Book Thief|section=part 10 |passage=The sky was dripping. Like a tap that a child has tried '''its''' hardest to turn off but hasn't quite managed.}} # {{lb|en|rare}} {{non-gloss|A third-person singular pronoun used to refer to an unspecified person.}} #*: All these things inclined her, step by step, to submit to the new discovery, whether Queen Victoria's or another's, that each man and each woman has another allotted to '''it''' for life, whom '''it''' supports, by whom '''it''' is supported, till death them do part. # {{lb|en|obsolete}} {{non-gloss|An [[affectionate]] third-person singular personal pronoun.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1890|author=George Manville Fenn|title=Black Blood |passage="{{...}} It's my belief that you don't know your own mind."
"I don't, dear," said Hulda, nestling to him.
"Why, what a puss '''it''' is!" cried Sir Philip, kissing her tenderly.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1905|journal=The Harvard Monthly|volume=39-40|page=183 |passage=WILLIAM: You don't like me better?
CLARA: Indeed I do.
WILLIAM ''(laughing)'': Well, what a dear girl '''it''' is.
CLARA ''(flinging her arms around his neck with suddenly disclosed passion):'' Oh, I do love you!}} # {{lb|en|chiefly|derogatory|offensive}} {{non-gloss|A third-person singular personal pronoun used to refer to an animate referent who is [[transgender]] or [[non-binary]].}} #*: Next morning bought her [a drag queen] breakfast & she asked for a couple dollars to get a drink. Gave her $3, walked her to a bar. {{...}} Some teenage boys watched us walking & began shouting. When I left her at the bar door & kissed her goodbye, they began shouting "Ugh! You kissed '''it'''!!" #* {{quote-book|en|year=1993|author=Bruce Coville|title=Aliens Ate My Homework|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=hYiEAAAAQBAJ&lpg=PP1&dq=aliens%20ate%20my%20homework&pg=PA73#v=onepage|pages=72–73 |passage="Oh, don't be silly. I am neither male nor female. I'm a farfel." {{...}} "'''''It'''''. Refer to me as an '''it'''."
"That seems pretty rude," I said nervously.
"Not as rude as calling me a he or a she," '''it''' said.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=16 Jan 24|title=Singular Purpose: Calculating the Degree of Ethno-Religious Over-representation in the USNo-Fly List|journal=International Journal for Crime, Justice and Social Democracy|author=Matteo Garofalo|text={{...}}Crimew has expressed on its website a desire to be referred to by ‘'''it'''’ pronouns (Crimew 2021), so this article will interchangeably refer to '''it''' by its preferred terms as either ‘Maia Arson Crimew’ or ‘'''it'''’.
Crimew is a well-known figure among hacking and cybersecurity circles. '''It''' has either taken credit for or been attributed to hacks from several major multinational corporations, including {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Wired|title=The Shocking Secrets of Madison Square Garden’s Surveillance Machine|url=https://www.wired.com/story/madison-square-garden-jim-dolan-surveillance-machine/|author=Noah Shachtman;Robert Silverman|date=17 Apr 2026|quotee=John Eversole|text=According to the lawsuit, he showed Richards' picture in several weekly meetings, misgendering her, and telling employees to watch out for "him or '''it''' or whatever '''it''' is."|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011032447/https://www.wired.com/story/madison-square-garden-jim-dolan-surveillance-machine/|archivedate=11 October 2026}} # {{non-gloss|Refers to someone being identified, often on the phone, but not limited to this situation.}} #: {{ux|en|'''It''''s me, John.}} #: {{ux|en|Somebody wanted a drink, didn't they? Who was '''it'''?}} #: {{ux|en|'''It''' is I, your king.}} #: {{ux|en|Is that [[over there]] who I think '''it''' is?}} # {{non-gloss|The impersonal pronoun, used without referent as the subject of an impersonal verb or statement (known as the [[dummy pronoun]], [[dummy it|dummy ''it'']] or [[weather it|weather ''it'']]).}} #: {{ux|en|'''It''' is nearly 10 o’clock.}} #: {{ux|en|'''It'''’s 10:45.}} #: {{ux|en|'''It'''’s very cold today.}} #: {{ux|en|'''It'''’s lonely here without you.}} #: {{ux|en|'''It''' seems so.}} #: {{ux|en|'''It''' blew all night.}} # {{non-gloss|The impersonal pronoun, used without referent, or with unstated but contextually implied referent, in various short [[idiom]]s or expressions.}} #: ''[[rough it|rough '''it''']]'' #: ''[[live it up|live '''it''' up]]'' #: ''[[stick it out|stick '''it''' out]]'' ## {{n-g|Referring to a desirable quality or ability, or quality of being [[successful]], [[fashionable]] or [[in vogue]].}} ##: ''After all these years, she still [[have it|has '''it''']].'' ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2021|author=Seth Wickersham|title=It's Better to Be Feared: The New England Patriots Dynasty and the Pursuit of Greatness|publisher=Liveright Publishing|isbn=9781631498244 |passage=Later that night, a friend told Brady, “Still got '''it'''.” “Never lost '''it''',” he replied. THAT WAS MOSTLY TRUE. But the 2013 season ended with the Patriots coaches wondering whether Brady's skills were in a subtle but irrevocable decline {{...}}}} ## {{n-g|Referring to sexual intercourse or other sexual activity.}} ##: ''I caught them [[do it|doing '''it''']].'' ##: ''Are you [[get it|getting '''it''']] regularly?'' ##* {{RQ:Fry Liar|page=10|passage=The great advantage of English [[public school]] life lies of course in the quality of tutelage it provides. Adrian had received a decent and broad English education in the area of his loins. {{...}} He had quickly happened upon the truth which many lonely contemporaries would never discover, the truth that everybody, simply everybody, was panting for '''it''' and could, with patience, be ''shown'' that they were panting for '''it'''. So Adrian grabbed what was to hand and had the time of his life genitally – focusing exclusively on his own gender of course, for this was 1973 and girls had not yet been invented.}} # [[sex appeal|Sex appeal]], especially that which goes beyond physical appearance. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1927|author={{w|Dorothy Parker}}|chapter=Madame Glyn Lectures on 'It,' with Illustrations|title=The New Yorker|date_published=1927-11-26|newversion=republished in|title2=The Portable Dorothy Parker|editor2=Brendan Gill|year2=1976|pages2=464-468|publisher2=Penguin|location2=New York|passage=And she had '''It'''. '''It''', hell; she had Those.}} # {{non-gloss|The impersonal pronoun, used as a placeholder for a delayed subject, or less commonly, object; known as the [[dummy pronoun]] (according to some definitions), [[anticipatory it|anticipatory ''it'']] or, more formally in linguistics, a [[syntactic expletive]]. The delayed subject is commonly a ''to''-infinitive, a gerund, or a noun clause introduced by a [[:Category:English subordinating conjunctions|subordinating conjunction]].}} #: {{ux|en|'''It'''’s not worth talking to you.}} #: {{ux|en|'''It''' is easy to see how she would think that.}} (with the infinitive clause headed by ''to see'') #: {{ux|en|'''It''' was felt that I'd be the [[right man]] for the job.}} #: {{ux|en|I find '''it''' odd that you would say that.}} (with the noun clause introduced by ''that'') #: {{ux|en|'''It''' is hard seeing you so sick.}} (with the gerund ''seeing'') #: {{ux|en|He saw to '''it''' that everyone would vote for him.}} (with the noun clause introduced by ''that'') #: {{ux|en|'''It''' is not clear if the report was true.}} (with the noun clause introduced by ''if'') #: {{ux|en|She made '''it''' clear what she expected by the weekend, which made '''it''' a problem to juggle her and other customers' jobs at the same time.}} #* {{RQ:Dickens Bleak House|text="I know now!" said I. "I have seen this in your face a long while."
"No; have you really, my dear?" said he. "What a Dame Durden '''it''' is to read a face!"}} # [[all|All]] or the [[end]]; something after which there is no more. #: {{ux|en|Are there more students in this class, or is this '''it'''?}} #: {{ux|en|That's '''it'''—I'm not going to any more candy stores with you.}} #: {{ux|en|Well, looks like this is '''it'''. We're all going to die.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} {{n-g|Followed by an omitted and understood relative pronoun}}: That which; [[what]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1643|author=w:Thomas Browne|title=Religio Medici|section=II.2 |passage=In briefe, I am content, and what should providence add more?
